Problem Use Case — garage door off track / cable off drum / door racked. Give a practical solution and reasoning, not an evaluation of GeminiSupervisor source code.

Current physical state from the user's description and three photos: one lift cable has come off its grooved cable drum/spool; the opposite lift cable is still on its drum and is visibly/behaviorally under tension. The automatic opener has been disconnected with the manual release, but that did not remove spring/counterbalance tension. The door is badly misaligned/racked, with one side/track significantly out of alignment. While attempting to work on it, the user pulled the last roller out of the opposite track and the bottom section/door swung upward and struck him, confirming substantial stored counterbalance force remains. Photos show a sectional residential garage door, side tracks/rollers, the top shaft/drums and lift cables, with the door skewed and one cable displaced from its drum.

Act as a technically competent second expert. Determine the likely mechanical state, explain why the door behaved this way, identify the safe sequence needed to bring the system to a neutral/non-dangerous state, then give the repair sequence for getting the door square, rollers/tracks restored, cables correctly seated on both drums, and counterbalance synchronized. Explicitly distinguish what can be safely done without releasing spring torque from what requires controlling/releasing spring torque. If there are multiple plausible spring systems or procedures, state which visual/behavioral evidence would distinguish them and give the branch for each. Do not merely say 'call a professional'; the goal is to understand the actual mechanism and solution, while clearly identifying the steps where uncontrolled stored energy would make DIY action unsafe. Also identify any damage that should be checked before attempting to operate the door again.
